findings.title: Task 2's "suite passes unchanged" success criterion is unsatisfiable
findings.description: Task 2 adds four `SnapshotMetric` members and simultaneously pins `PythonAdapter.metrics` to the explicit old four, with Success: "the full `tests/metrology/` suite passes unchanged." But `tests/metrology/snapshot/test_python_length.py:60` asserts `adapter.metrics == set(SnapshotMetric)`; once the enum has eight members and the adapter declares four, that assertion fails. The task must authorize the one-line assertion edit (e.g., to the explicit four-metric set) or the Task 2 commit gate cannot be met as written.

findings.title: Task 7's `FunctionLength` rename breaks `test_render.py`, which its success criterion doesn't name
findings.description: Task 7 renames `FunctionLength` → `MeasuredFunction` and adds a required `complexity: int` field, with Success scoped to "400's length tests pass … edited only for the rename." However `tests/metrology/snapshot/test_render.py#python_snapshot` imports `FunctionLength` from `lengths` and constructs it positionally (`FunctionLength("a.py", "f", 1, 70)`), so after Task 7 that file fails import/collection — a render test, not a length test. Add `test_render.py` to Task 7's edit list (rename the import and supply a `complexity` value) so the Task 7 commit leaves the touched-area suite green.

findings.title: Commit checkpoints are checkboxes and sit at tested points
findings.description: All 18 commit markers are `- [ ] Commit: …` checkboxes rather than plain lines. That matches AGENTS.md's explicit rule that every task-file item is a checkbox and the completed slice-400 task file's convention, and each marker follows a task whose success criteria include passing tests, so checkpoints land at working, tested states. No change required.
